note: 23 October 2026: the grocer's front worn the way the tea rooms', the newsagent's, the ironmonger's and Rita's passed (tools/art-recipes/front_wear.py, the same settings), with this front's own places read from its model on 23 October. Its shop door stands at the back of a recessed lobby (y 0.53, x -2.546 to -1.748, at the viewer's left), its bronze pull at x -2.575, 0.78 to 1.12 up, on the door's left stile; the lobby's cream cheek (x -2.65 to -2.63) beside it. Its paints are the cream render (pilasters x -3.0 to -2.65 and 2.65 to 3.0, their plinths 0 to 0.6 up and 0.18 proud; the cornice; the lobby cheek), the bronze of the window, sill and door (paint_bronze_plate) and the green slab stallriser (x -1.642 to 2.648, 0 to 0.505, chrome-capped). Only the cream chips: the green slab takes dirt and splash, not chips, so every chip region names its paint. The bronze is left clean (try 1 of the bake, 23 October: front_wear bakes colour and roughness only and writes the paint non-metallic, so the bronze, metallic 0.9, came out flat brown paint; a bronze kick plate and sill kept bright by feet and cleaning is the period's norm). No lock-rail or sill chips (the tea rooms' and the ironmonger's lesson: chips along a rail read as a dotted frame). No night glow: its fascia is glass lettered in its own picture.
texture_px_note: one texture set per paint, its ground filled with the clean paint (Rita's lesson)

chip_regions.name: the left pilaster's plinth, by the lobby

roughness_note: 22 October, the ironmonger's gate from the right: grime at roughness 0.85 caught the sky as a grey sheen at a low slant; street grime here is damp splash, so it is only a little duller than the paint.
